title: attest_peer is never called; its documented uid check is not enforced
description:
persona-grpc/src/consumer_attest.rs:16 `attest_peer` carries this doc:

    ## Security
    uid is verified against the daemon's own uid. Connections from other
    uids are rejected.

Grep across the workspace finds no caller. The only references to `attest_peer` are its own two definitions (linux and non-linux) and the `pub mod consumer_attest;` in persona-grpc/src/lib.rs:3. persona-grpc/src/server.rs:37-41 hands the raw `UnixListenerStream` straight to `Server::builder().serve_with_incoming()` without inspecting any peer, and service.rs:187 confirms it: "consumer_uid via SO_PEERCRED not yet plumbed through tonic".

So the SO_PEERCRED uid check, the `/proc/{pid}/exe` hash, and the whole `ConsumerIdentity` attestation path are unreachable. Every connection that reaches the socket gets an SVID.

The socket mode is 0600 (server.rs:32), which is the actual access control today — but note server.rs:27-32 binds first and chmods second, so there is a window at the default umask where another local uid can connect, and nothing behind that window checks who connected.

What goes wrong if left: the doc comment asserts an enforcement that does not exist, which is worse than no doc — a reader auditing this daemon will read consumer_attest.rs and conclude peer attestation is in place. Either wire `attest_peer` into the accept loop, or change the doc to state plainly that the function is not yet called and link the tracking issue.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.41 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
